## I4 functional architecture

The frozen HFT baseline contains two order-data producers that can reach R01. Both are now modeled through one integration-owned boundary:

```text
ordinary bridge order_data ----\
                                -> prebuild-priority mux
R01 prebuild order_data --------/          |
                                           v
                                  shared futures risk
                                  - CL admission
                                  - committed EX
                                  - one state owner
                                  - one AMU owner
                                           |
                                     ACCEPT only
                                           v
                              frozen financial_protocol_encoder
                                           |
                                          R01
```

`ENABLE_R01_PREBUILD=1` in the frozen XGMII-oriented baseline means the prebuild path must be gated; ordinary-bridge-only interception is not acceptable.

## Functional evidence closed in CI

I4 self-checking regression now proves:

- BUY OPEN admission creates reservation plus order context;
- committed full fill mutates the same futures state and removes context;
- a later SELL CLOSE succeeds only because the shared state now contains long inventory;
- committed execution wins simultaneous EX/CL owner acquisition;
- the losing CL transaction remains backpressured until the EX transaction completes;
- ordinary and prebuild producers both traverse risk;
- prebuild retains source priority;
- kill-switch reject never reaches the encoder contract;
- accepted 256-bit payload is not rewritten.

## Remaining I4 local gates

Run in this order after pulling the branch:

```powershell
pwsh .\scripts\run_i4_r01_parity_xsim.ps1
pwsh .\scripts\run_i4_r01_path_ooc_impl.ps1
```

The XSim test instantiates two copies of the pinned frozen `financial_protocol_encoder`: one direct baseline and one behind the integrated risk path. It compares the complete 80-byte R01 for legacy and prebuild accepted orders and requires no packet for a kill-switch reject.

The OOC flow uses the real pinned RMIC XPM AMU, shared futures state, dual-source order boundary, and pinned frozen HFT encoder. Acceptance is full route at 6.400 ns with real BRAM, WNS >= 0, TNS = 0, zero routing errors, and reviewed utilization/DRC/power/critical path.
